points.description: The answer conveys that the compiler replaces each call to the inline function with a copy of the function's code at that call site (the body is duplicated wherever the function is called). Equivalent wording such as 'the function body is inserted/expanded in place of every call' earns the mark.

rubric.notes: The model answer is a single idea, so the scheme has one all-or-nothing point worth the full 5 marks. Full marks go to any answer stating that the function's code is copied or expanded at every call site. No marks go to answers that describe inlining only vaguely (for example, 'it makes the function faster') or that describe a normal function call without the copying.
